plain: The Philadelphia Experiment, a legendary secret experiment said to have taken place around Philadelphia and Norfolk, Virginia, in 1943, was real, Jesse Michels argues, and it was run by a man named Thomas Townsend Brown, who he says had a nervous breakdown around that time. Michels tells this himself across several episodes, pointing to an FBI file on Brown from 1942 and 1943 and to the researcher Bill Moore, and he says Brown told a friend named Josh Reynolds late in life that the experiment 'did happen, its events were just greatly exaggerated.' Michels tells it differently from one episode to another: sometimes Brown 'led' or 'ran' the project, and once he calls the popular story a 'wacky' cover over 'a real thing going on.'
